title: What Survives the Experiment
preservation_note: Do not discard or relabel source assets. Research figures and recordings remain attributed in the linked source pages. No experimental outcomes invented.

scenes.title: The anatomy room
scenes.subtitle: 2011 / School
scenes.narration: My first anatomy lesson was not a drawing. A fox lay on the table. I wanted to understand how its parts worked together.
scenes.credit: Personal photographic archive; school anatomy lesson, 2011

scenes.title: A microscope of my own
scenes.subtitle: Cairo → Qatar
scenes.narration: Later, I brought a microscope from Cairo to Qatar. At home, curiosity did not have to wait for laboratory hours.

scenes.title: Beginning with matter
scenes.subtitle: Early chemistry
scenes.narration: We began with plant extracts and questions about medicinal chemistry. Some experiments were simple. The answers were rarely as simple.
scenes.credit: Archived chemistry photograph and original apparatus recording; not a recording of the extracts experiment

scenes.title: What a spectrum can say
scenes.subtitle: Imine chemistry / Molecular sensing
scenes.narration: Imine synthesis and molecular sensing taught me to distrust a beautiful explanation until I could interrogate the spectrum.
scenes.credit: Published scientific figure from the research record; attribution in the Figures archive

scenes.title: Learning in company
scenes.subtitle: QUACS / Scientific community
scenes.narration: We built a student chemistry community. Science grew in shared laboratories, long arguments, and the people who challenged our assumptions.
scenes.credit: Photographic archive: encounter with Professor Elmostafa El-Sayed and colleagues, 2017

scenes.title: When the polymer resisted
scenes.subtitle: Materials / Unfinished experiments
scenes.narration: A polymer would not behave as planned. I learned how little a plausible structure tells us about a real material.
scenes.credit: Original record of unsuccessful polymer trials; no successful dissolution is claimed

scenes.title: A living system moves
scenes.subtitle: Zebrafish / Microscopy
scenes.narration: Then I began following developing vessels in zebrafish. The organism moved, blood flowed, and measurement became a different problem.
scenes.credit: Original zebrafish cardiovascular microscopy; not direct evidence of every claim in the narration

scenes.title: The section that failed
scenes.subtitle: 2% agarose / Paraffin
scenes.narration: An embedding attempt failed when agarose and paraffin would not hold together. The microtome exposed a materials problem, not a usable section.

scenes.title: An airway reopens
scenes.subtitle: Pulmonary mechanobiology
scenes.narration: In the lung, we studied what happens when an airway reopens and a moving interface injures epithelial cells.
scenes.credit: Published flow-chamber research figure; controlled epithelial injury, not clinical evidence

scenes.title: The interface matters
scenes.subtitle: Biomaterials / Surfaces
scenes.narration: Biomaterials and engineered surfaces added another constraint: a substance can be chemically interesting yet behave very differently at an interface.
scenes.credit: Published materials-research imagery; source and figure context in the research record

scenes.title: Reaching the lung
scenes.subtitle: MSc / Inhalable vesicles
scenes.narration: Now I study dexamethasone vesicles intended for inhalation. A carrier must withstand nebulization before it can even be assessed for delivery.
scenes.credit: Pulmonary research-context illustration; ongoing thesis, not a claim of demonstrated clinical delivery

scenes.title: What can be relied upon?
scenes.subtitle: Pharmaceutical history / Continuing research
scenes.narration: I also study how earlier pharmacists made medicines dependable. Across centuries and disciplines, I keep returning to what the evidence can actually bear.
scenes.credit: Contemporary portrait and editorial typography; not a historical manuscript facsimile
